mechanism: KH631 is an adeno-associated viral vector gene therapy delivered by intraocular or subretinal injection that contains coding sequence for an anti-VEGF human VEGF receptor fusion protein, intended to provide sustained intraocular anti-VEGF expression after one administration.
phase: U.S. Phase 1; China Phase 1/2 on ClinicalTrials.gov and China Phase II per 2025 Kanghong annual report
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists VAN-2201 (NCT05657301) as an active, not recruiting U.S. Phase 1 open-label, multicenter, dose-escalating study of one-time KH631 intraocular injection in 25 previously anti-VEGF-treated participants with neovascular AMD, with estimated primary completion in September 2026 and estimated study completion in September 2027. A separate China ClinicalTrials.gov record (NCT05672121) is recruiting 42 subjects in a Phase 1/2 open-label dose-escalation study, with estimated completion December 28, 2026. Kanghong's 2025 annual report states KH631 is in China Phase II and U.S. Phase I, with partial China Phase I results shared at ARVO 2025.
expected_launch_window: 2030-2033 if early KH631 data support pivotal development and regulatory filing; no approval date disclosed
clinical_summary: KH631 targets the core wet AMD VEGF pathway but attempts to replace frequent intravitreal anti-VEGF injections with sustained anti-VEGF expression after one subretinal or intraocular gene-therapy administration. Preclinical non-human-primate data showed retinal retention, suppression of grade IV CNV lesions at doses as low as 3 x 10^8 vg/eye, and transgene expression for more than 96 weeks. Kanghong reported that partial China Phase I findings were shared at ARVO 2025 and that the first low-dose patient required no rescue treatment within 2 years after KH631 injection. Public ClinicalTrials.gov records have no posted results, and the U.S. program remains Phase 1, so the treatment-burden hypothesis is promising but not yet supported by controlled human efficacy data.
safety_summary: NCT05657301 and NCT05672121 are designed primarily around ocular and systemic AEs/SAEs through 52 and 104 weeks, but neither record has posted results. The clinical records require prior anti-VEGF response and exclude several higher-risk ocular histories. Subretinal AAV analog Luxturna labeling highlights procedure- and product-associated ocular risks including endophthalmitis, permanent visual acuity decline, retinal abnormalities, increased intraocular pressure, air-bubble precautions, cataract, and common ocular adverse reactions such as conjunctival hyperemia, cataract, increased intraocular pressure, retinal tear, macular hole, eye inflammation, eye pain, and maculopathy. KH631-specific human safety remains an evidence gap pending full trial readout.
management_tools: Keep KH631 on a high-cost ophthalmic gene-therapy watchlist rather than routine wet AMD formulary action until Phase 1/2 results and pivotal plans are public
Plan for medical-benefit management with prior authorization, not standard pharmacy-benefit dispensing
Require confirmed neovascular AMD diagnosis, eye-specific baseline BCVA/OCT documentation, and prior response to intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy
Require retina specialist or qualified ocular gene-therapy center administration with site-of-care review
Limit use to one administration per treated eye unless repeat dosing is supported by final labeling and evidence
Use eye-specific outcome tracking for BCVA, central retinal thickness, rescue anti-VEGF injections, ocular inflammation, retinal detachment or tear, and cataract events
Evaluate outcomes-based contracting, warranty, or episode-payment models if final price resembles ophthalmic gene-therapy analogs
Maintain preferred standard anti-VEGF pathway and rescue-treatment criteria until KH631 demonstrates durable outcomes versus current anti-VEGF options
evidence_gaps: No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results for NCT05657301 or NCT05672121.
No FDA approval, U.S. label, BLA filing date, or U.S. pivotal study was found.
The public U.S. trial remains Phase 1 and uncontrolled; the China record is Phase 1/2, while Kanghong's 2025 annual report describes KH631 as China Phase II.
Kanghong reports partial China Phase I ARVO 2025 findings and a no-rescue-treatment observation in the first low-dose patient, but full peer-reviewed human efficacy and safety results were not found.
No direct KH631 price exists; annual cost estimate uses Luxturna, an approved subretinal ocular AAV gene therapy, as the closest public price analog.
Final KH631 administration setting, procedure costs, corticosteroid regimen, retreatment policy, bilateral-eye use, and net payer cost are unknown.

sources.title: Safety and Tolerability of KH631 Gene Therapy in Participants With Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration
supports: Official title is a Phase I, open-label, multicenter, dose-escalating study of KH631 gene therapy in participants with neovascular AMD.
Lead sponsor is Chengdu Origen Biotechnology Co., Ltd.; organization is Chengdu Kanghong Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd.; study ID is VAN-2201.
Overall status is active, not recruiting; actual start was 2023-10-16; estimated primary completion is 2026-09; estimated completion is 2027-09.
Estimated enrollment is 25 subjects across five dose cohorts receiving one-time KH631 intraocular injection.
KH631 is described as an AAV vector containing coding sequence for an anti-VEGF protein.
Primary outcomes are ocular/systemic AEs and SAEs and change in BCVA through 52 weeks; secondary outcomes include safety, rescue injections, and BCVA through 104 weeks.
Brief summary states KH631 is designed to deliver a protein that targets and blocks VEGF and could reduce regular intraocular injection burden.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Safety and Tolerability of KH631 Gene Therapy in Subjects With Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration (nAMD)
supports: Official title is a Phase I/II, open-label, multiple-cohort, dose-escalation study of KH631 gene therapy in subjects with neovascular AMD.
Lead sponsor is Chengdu Origen Biotechnology Co., Ltd.; study ID is KH631-40101.
Overall status is recruiting; actual start was 2023-02-06; estimated primary completion and study completion are 2026-12-28.
Estimated enrollment is 42 subjects in China across five KH631 subretinal injection dose cohorts.
KH631 is described as an AAV vector containing coding sequence for an anti-VEGF protein and as a one-time subretinal injection.

Primary outcomes include safety through 24 weeks and BCVA change through 52 weeks; secondary outcomes include safety, BCVA, central retinal thickness, leakage by FFA, and rescue injections through 104 weeks.
Exploratory outcomes measure KH631 protein and VEGF-A in aqueous fluid and blood through 104 weeks.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Chengdu Kanghong Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. 2025 Annual Report
supports: Kanghong states KH631 ophthalmic injection for neovascular/wet AMD is in China Phase II and U.S. Phase I.
Kanghong describes KH631 as an internally developed gene-therapy innovative product from its controlled subsidiary Chengdu Hongji/Origen Biotechnology and as a Class 1 therapeutic biologic in China.
KH631 is based on a proprietary AAV delivery system and showed sustained efficacy in preclinical disease models.
Kanghong states KH631 received China clinical trial approval in November 2022 and U.S. FDA clearance by email in November 2022 to conduct the corresponding nAMD clinical study.
Kanghong states partial China Phase I results were shared at ARVO 2025 and the first low-dose patient required no rescue treatment within 2 years after KH631 injection.
Kanghong states KH631 also received China clinical trial approval in January 2026 for diabetic macular edema.

sources.title: Chengdu Origen and Vanotech Announce First Patient Dosed in VAN-2201 Phase 1 Trial of Gene Therapy for Wet Age-Related Macular Degeneration
supports: Chengdu Origen and Vanotech announced first patient dosing in the VAN-2201 multicenter Phase 1 clinical trial of KH631 for wet AMD.
The U.S. open-label dose-escalation trial evaluates safety, tolerability, and efficacy of KH631 as a single-administration gene therapy in previously treated wet AMD patients.
KH631 is described as a recombinant adeno-associated virus vector encoding a human VEGF receptor fusion protein.
The companies stated KH631 is designed to deliver anti-VEGF continuously to the retina, with potential to reduce the burden of regular intraocular injections.
The trial was expected to include approximately 25 previously treated wet AMD subjects responsive to anti-VEGF therapy.

sources.title: Preclinical evaluation of KH631, a novel rAAV8 gene therapy product for neovascular age-related macular degeneration
supports: KH631 is a recombinant adeno-associated virus 8 vector encoding a human VEGF receptor fusion protein being developed as a long-term treatment for nAMD.
The article states frequent anti-VEGF intravitreal injections are standard treatment for nAMD and create burden for patients, families, and providers.
In non-human primate preclinical studies, subretinal KH631 at 3 x 10^8 vg/eye produced retinal retention of the transgene product and prevented formation and progression of grade IV CNV lesions.
Sustained transgene expression was observed for more than 96 weeks.
Authors concluded single subretinal KH631 injection could potentially offer a one-time, low-dose treatment for nAMD.
Several authors were Chengdu Origen Biotechnology employees, and Chengdu Origen funded the study.

sources.title: DailyMed: LUXTURNA (voretigene neparvovec-rzyl) intraocular suspension for subretinal injection
supports: Luxturna is an AAV vector-based gene therapy for subretinal injection and is administered once per eye on separate days.
Label warnings include endophthalmitis, permanent decline in visual acuity, retinal abnormalities, increased intraocular pressure, expansion of intraocular air bubbles, and cataract.

Most common adverse reactions in clinical trials included conjunctival hyperemia, cataract, increased intraocular pressure, retinal tear, dellen, macular hole, subretinal deposits, eye inflammation, eye irritation, eye pain, and maculopathy.
The label recommends peri-administration systemic oral corticosteroids.

sources.title: Spark's gene therapy price tag: $850,000
supports: Nature Biotechnology reported Spark priced Luxturna at $850,000 total, or $425,000 per eye.
Luxturna is an approved retinal gene therapy and is used as the closest public price analog for KH631 because no KH631 price is available.

sources.title: DailyMed: EYLEA (aflibercept) injection, solution
supports: Eylea is indicated for neovascular/wet AMD.
Recommended nAMD dosing is 2 mg intravitreal injection monthly for the first 3 months, followed by every 8 weeks; some patients may need monthly dosing after the first 12 weeks.
Eylea labeling illustrates current anti-VEGF treatment burden that KH631 aims to reduce.
Warnings include endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, retinal vasculitis, and increased intraocular pressure after intravitreal injections.

sources.title: Eylea Prices, Coupons, Copay Cards and Patient Assistance
supports: Drugs.com listed Eylea 40 mg/mL intravitreal solution from $1,962.09 for 0.05 mL.
Eylea price is used only as a standard anti-VEGF comparator context, not as the KH631 annual cost estimate.

sources.title: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0927: Voretigene Neparvovec-rzyl (Luxturna)
supports: Aetna requires precertification for Luxturna and identifies it as a Gene-based, Cellular & Other Innovative Therapies product receiving dedicated review.
Policy requires administration at an Aetna GCIT network unless the plan does not require it.
Luxturna must be prescribed by or in consultation with an ophthalmologist.
Coverage is for one-time administration per eye when criteria are met; repeat administration in the same eye is considered experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Policy requires disease-confirming testing, viable retinal cells, and no previous Luxturna treatment course.

sources.title: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0701: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Inhibitors for Ocular Indications
supports: Aetna requires precertification for ocular VEGF inhibitors including Eylea, Eylea HD, Beovu, Vabysmo, Lucentis, and Susvimo in applicable plans.
Aetna considers intravitreal aflibercept medically necessary for neovascular/wet AMD when criteria are met.

Aetna considers continuation of ocular VEGF inhibitor therapy medically necessary when the member demonstrates positive clinical response such as improvement or maintenance in BCVA or visual field, reduced rate of vision decline, or reduced risk of more severe vision loss.

Susvimo criteria require prior response to at least two intravitreal VEGF inhibitor injections within the past 6 months, illustrating payer use of prior anti-VEGF response criteria for durable ocular delivery approaches.

expected_launch_window.value: 2030-2033 if early KH631 data support pivotal development and regulatory filing; no approval date disclosed
expected_launch_window.method: Used the U.S. Phase 1 estimated primary completion in 2026, estimated study completion in 2027, the China Phase II status disclosed in the 2025 annual report, absence of posted results, and expected need for pivotal wet AMD gene-therapy studies plus regulatory review.
expected_launch_window.explanation: KH631 has early clinical momentum, but the U.S. program is still Phase 1 and no pivotal U.S. trial or filing date is public, so a launch before 2030 appears unlikely.

annual_cost_range.method: Used Luxturna, an approved one-time subretinal ocular AAV gene therapy, as the closest public price analog: $425,000 per eye and $850,000 for bilateral treatment.
annual_cost_range.explanation: No KH631 price is available. The estimate reflects potential first-year gross drug acquisition cost for one or both eyes and excludes surgery, facility, anesthesia, corticosteroids, monitoring, rescue anti-VEGF injections, rebates, discounts, outcomes-based rebates, and net payer adjustments.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced KH631's one-time anti-VEGF gene-therapy approach, preclinical durability beyond 96 weeks, company-reported 2-year no-rescue observation in the first low-dose China Phase I patient, and the lack of controlled posted human results.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: If durable rescue-free control is confirmed, KH631 could materially reduce injection burden versus standard anti-VEGF therapy, but evidence is still early and subretinal administration adds procedural complexity.

budget_impact.method: Assessed likely one-time gene-therapy pricing from the Luxturna analog against a prevalent wet AMD population and existing recurring anti-VEGF spend.
budget_impact.explanation: Even with restricted use, first-year per-eye cost could be high if priced like retinal gene-therapy analogs; payer exposure would depend heavily on eligible-eye criteria, bilateral use, contracts, and durability versus avoided anti-VEGF injections.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from early U.S. Phase 1 status, China Phase II progress, high potential per-patient cost, possible shift from chronic anti-VEGF injections to one-time gene therapy, and the need for specialized administration.
disruption_risk.explanation: KH631 is not near U.S. launch, but it could create meaningful medical-benefit, site-of-care, contracting, and outcome-tracking work if clinical durability is confirmed.

recommended_action.method: Recommended action reflects early U.S. development, no posted trial results, no filing date, and high but still uncertain future payer impact.
recommended_action.explanation: Monitor for full ARVO/publication results, U.S. Phase 1 completion, pivotal design, durability and rescue-injection data, and pricing signals before payer buildout beyond watchlist and analog policy planning.

quality_flags: No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results for either KH631 nAMD record as of the latest checked records.
Development-stage mismatch to track: ClinicalTrials.gov lists the China study as Phase 1/2, while Kanghong's 2025 annual report describes KH631 for nAMD as China Phase II and U.S. Phase I.

Sponsor/manufacturer naming requires normalization: ClinicalTrials.gov lead sponsor is Chengdu Origen Biotechnology Co., Ltd.; the organization field is Chengdu Kanghong Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd.; Kanghong's report describes KH631 as developed by its controlled subsidiary Chengdu Hongji/Origen Biotechnology.
Human efficacy evidence is immature; the strongest public efficacy evidence is preclinical plus company-reported partial China Phase I ARVO 2025 observations.
Annual cost estimate is analog-based from Luxturna and may materially differ from final KH631 pricing, dosing, contracting, bilateral use, and administration costs.
KH631 is not FDA-approved or marketed for wet AMD; do not treat as a launched product.
